issues.legal_issue: Land used before statutory vesting as appurtenant property or for facilities connected with an existing industrial undertaking does not vest in the state or village body when the applicable saving provisions preserve the relevant rights.
material_facts: Before the vesting date, part of the disputed land was appurtenant to the mill’s staff quarters, and other parts were used for molasses and sullage-water tanks and related industrial purposes.
The consolidation authorities found that the mill had used and possessed the land for those purposes; those findings were not set aside.
The village land management body later executed a lease of the plots in favour of the person claiming tenure rights.
issues.conclusion: The plots did not vest in the state and therefore could not subsequently vest in the village body; the village body had no authority to lease them, and the lease could not confer rights on the lessee.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 4 and 6 of the U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, estate property vested in the state subject to statutory savings. Section 7(aa) preserved qualifying easement or similar rights for the more beneficial enjoyment of land, and Section 9 preserved buildings and their appurtenant sites. Under Section 117, only property that had vested in the state could be vested in the Gaon Sabha. Sections 195 and 198 governed the Land Management Committee’s authority and preferences in admitting persons to land; they did not empower it to allot land that had never vested in the Gaon Sabha. Sections 28-A and 28-B of the U.P. Panchayat Raj Act described the committee’s duties concerning village property.

rule.if: consolidation_proceeding and prevesting_appurtenant_or_industrial_use and use_findings_undisturbed and village_body_granted_lease

predicates.consolidation_proceeding: The dispute was considered in proceedings under a land-consolidation system.
predicates.prevesting_appurtenant_or_industrial_use: Before statutory vesting, the disputed land was appurtenant to existing buildings or was used for facilities connected with an existing industrial undertaking.
predicates.use_findings_undisturbed: The findings about the land’s pre-vesting use were not set aside by the reviewing authorities.
predicates.village_body_granted_lease: A village body granted a lease of the disputed land to a person claiming rights through that lease.
predicates.village_body_lease_conveys_no_title: A lease granted by the village body does not convey title to the disputed land.

issues.definition: When a consolidation dispute concerns land used before vesting as appurtenant property or for industrial facilities, the relevant use findings remain undisturbed, and a village body later grants a lease, that lease conveys no title.

issues.legal_issue: Consolidation authorities may determine whether a document relied on to claim rights is void and may disregard it when deciding the parties’ rights.
material_facts: The claimant sought tenure rights in consolidation proceedings on the basis of a lease executed by the village land management body.
The land had not vested in the state or the village body, so the body lacked authority to grant the lease.
The High Court held that the consolidation authorities could not examine the lease’s validity.
issues.conclusion: The lease was void from its inception, and its existence did not prevent the consolidation authorities from deciding the parties’ rights by disregarding it.
issues.legal_principle: In Gorakh Nath Dube v. Hari Narain Singh, the Court held that a void document liable to be ignored does not affect the jurisdiction of consolidation courts. The Court followed that principle in Dulari Devi v. Janardan Singh, Ashrafi Lal v. Koili, and Muneshwar v. Raja Mohammed Khan. It rejected the contrary approach of the Allahabad High Court’s Full Bench in Similesh Kumar v. Gaon Sabha, Uskar, Ghazipur, and applied the principle to the authorities’ adjudication of objections under the U.P. Consolidation of Holdings Act, 1953.

predicates.consolidation_proceeding: The dispute was before authorities deciding rights in land through a consolidation proceeding.
predicates.rights_claimed_through_document: A party relied on a document as the basis for its claimed rights in the land.
predicates.purported_grantor_lacked_authority: The person or body that purported to grant the document had no authority over the land.
predicates.consolidation_authorities_may_disregard_: The consolidation authorities may disregard a void document when deciding the parties’ rights.

issues.definition: When a party claims rights through a document in a consolidation proceeding and its purported grantor lacked authority, the authorities may disregard that document.

issues.legal_issue: The statutory consequences of failing to bring an ejectment suit do not apply to land that never vested in the state or village body.
material_facts: The mill possessed the disputed land and used it for appurtenant and industrial purposes before statutory vesting.
The disputed land did not vest in the state and consequently did not vest in the village body.
The High Court relied on the absence of an ejectment suit to reject the mill’s claim to rights in the land.
issues.conclusion: Neither Section 209 nor Section 210 applied because those provisions presupposed land belonging to a tenure holder or the Gaon Sabha, whereas the disputed land had never vested in the state or the Gaon Sabha.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 209 and 210 of the U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act address possession of land belonging to a bhumidhar, sirdar, asami, or Gaon Sabha and the consequences of failing to bring or execute an ejectment suit. The Court noted that the former clause of Section 210 that provided for acquiring sirdari status following failure to sue was not part of Section 210 as amended in 1976. The statutory provisions therefore could not supply a basis for tenure rights over land that had never vested in the relevant public body.

predicates.consolidation_proceeding: The claim was decided in a land-consolidation proceeding.
predicates.possession_claimed_on_land: A party relied on possession of the disputed land in asserting rights over it.
predicates.land_never_vested_in_village_body: The disputed land never vested in the village body.
predicates.ejectment_default_rules_do_not_apply: The statutory rules governing the consequences of failure to bring an ejectment suit do not apply to the disputed land.

issues.definition: When a possession-based claim is considered in a consolidation proceeding over land that never vested in the village body, the statutory ejectment-default rules do not apply.
